target_customer: Cities, transit agencies, campuses and ride-hail networks that buy autonomous shuttle and robotaxi service
problem: Public transit and short routes are costly to operate and underserved. May Mobility runs small autonomous shuttles on defined paths and manages operations end to end.
business_model: Autonomous vehicle service and technology licensing to transit agencies and ride-hail partners

founders.name: Edwin Olson
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page, worked on autonomous vehicles for over a decade including the 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge and vehicles for Ford and Toyota Research Institute.

exit.reason: SPAC merger with ACP Holdings Acquisition Corp announced September 16, 2026, targeting close by end of 2026; not yet completed.

competitors.name: Navya
competitors.what: French autonomous shuttle maker with larger shuttles
competitors.traction_then: Finished a year-long free demonstration in Las Vegas

competitors.name: Optimus Ride
competitors.what: Autonomous shuttles in Boston Seaport and planned communities
competitors.traction_then: Ran a service in Boston's Seaport

competitors.name: Drive.ai
competitors.traction_then: Three vehicles on a few routes in Arlington, Texas since October 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a safe self-driving system, even on defined routes, was research-grade work requiring perception, planning and vehicle integration, plus operations.

defensibility.rationale: Safety case, operating data and OEM partnerships are hard to replicate, but many well-funded AV players competed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals such as Drive.ai were absorbed (Apple acquired it in 2019 per a TechCrunch result) while May Mobility stayed independent and took Toyota and BMW strategic money.

market_need_then: In 2018 coverage, shuttle operators were launching pilots in several US cities and Detroit's first autonomous service ran in June 2018. Strategic investors BMW and Toyota funded the seed.

branding.community_and_virality: No source found for merch or fan communities. Press coverage was about technology and deployments.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is functional with partner-driven visibility (Toyota, Lyft, Uber), but no source ties growth to the brand itself.

pivots.from: Small shuttles on defined routes for cities and campuses
pivots.to: Autonomous ride-hail technology with Lyft, Uber and Grab
pivots.why: Company site now describes its system as driving ride-hail vehicles. The reason was not stated in sources opened.

outcome_analysis: May Mobility seeded with strategic backing from BMW and Toyota in February 2018 and kept raising through Series B in December 2019, Series C in 2022 and a 2023 round, reaching about $194M by July 2022. It expanded from shuttle pilots to driverless service and ride-hail partnerships. In September 2026 it announced a SPAC merger valuing it near $1.4B. The path shows strong team execution and strategic investor pull in a capital-heavy field.
notes: Wikipedia and a search summary name Alisyn Malek and Steve Vozar as co-founders, but the YC page and company site list only Edwin Olson, so they are not recorded as founders. Series A $22M is dated 2019 because the article only links to a February 2019 piece. Wikipedia dates the seed to December 2018 in text but cites a February 26, 2018 source, and TechCrunch confirms February 2018. The 2022 Series C is reported as $83M initial close (January 2022) then $111M by July 2022 with total $194M, which may overlap, and the $83M may be part of the $111M. Series D label appears in one result but is recorded as other. Competitor sources are 2018 coverage within a few months of the batch, and the Axios link is a wrapped Wired article.
